```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(here)

library(scales)

current_year <- 2026

# A) (optionally) update underlying data set with freshly downloaded data
dir.create(here("data-dynamic"), showWarnings = FALSE)
# MeteoSwiss data:
if (FALSE) { # NOTE: activate this for automatic update
  source(here("analysis", "00_download_meteoswiss_data.R")) 
  # creates: data-raw/meteoswiss_station_bern/Bern_cur_daily.csv and Bern_hist_daily.csv
  
  source(here("analysis", "01_calc_pcwd.R"))                
  # creates: data-dynamic/Bern_pcwd_daily.csv
} else {
  for (filename in c("Bern_pcwd_daily.csv")){
    file.copy(from = here("data/",         filename), 
              to   = here("data-dynamic/", filename), 
              overwrite = TRUE)
  }
}
# GECO-sites:
if (FALSE) { # NOTE: activate this for automatic update
  source(here("analysis", "03_GECOsites.R")) # TODO: this does not yet exist
  # creates: data-dynamic/daily_SWP_drakau.csv and daily_TWD_drakau.csv
} else {
  for (filename in c("daily_SWP_drakau.csv", "daily_TWD_drakau.csv")){
    file.copy(from = here("data/",         filename), 
              to   = here("data-dynamic/", filename), 
              overwrite = TRUE)
  }
}
# SwissEOVHI:
if (FALSE) { # NOTE: activate this for automatic update
  source(here("analysis", "02_swissEOVHI.R"))
  # creates: data-dynamic/swisseo_vhi_bern_plot_data.csv and swisseo_vhi_bern_stats.csv
} else {

    file.copy(from = here("data/",         filename), 
              to   = here("data-dynamic/", filename),

}
# ERA5-Land:

  source(here("analysis", "04_calc_pcwd_era5land.R"))
  # creates: data-dynamic/swisseo_vhi_bern_plot_data.csv and swisseo_vhi_bern_stats.csv
} else {
  for (filename in c("ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2026_r-generated_regionBern.nc",
                     "ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2026_r-generated_regionCH.nc",
                     "ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2026_r-generated_regionEUROPE.nc",
                     "ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2025_r-generated_regionBern.nc",
                     "ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2025_r-generated_regionCH.nc",
                     "ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2025_r-generated_regionEUROPE.nc"
                     )){
    file.copy(from = here("data/",         filename), 
              to   = here("data-dynamic/", filename),

}


# B) Load (updated) data
meteo_pcwd <- read_csv(here("data-dynamic", "Bern_pcwd_daily.csv"))

df_SWP <- read_csv(here("data-dynamic","daily_SWP_drakau.csv"))
df_TWD <- read_csv(here("data-dynamic","daily_TWD_drakau.csv"))

vhi_plot_data <- read_csv(here("data-dynamic", "swisseo_vhi_bern_plot_data.csv"))
vhi_stats <- read_csv(here("data-dynamic", "swisseo_vhi_bern_stats.csv"))
```

## Overview

Drought conditions have intensified across parts of Switzerland during spring and early summer 2026. A combination of below-average precipitation and increasing atmospheric evaporative demand has lead to signals of increasing drought stress since April.

This drought monitor combines several complementary indicators to assess the current drought situation: 
  - the potential cumulative water deficit (derived from local meteorological observations or ERA5-Land),
  - local soil water potential observations
  - tree water deficit observations
  - and satellite-based vegetation health metrics from swisstopo. 

The combinations of these indicators provides insights into the severity of ongoing dry conditions with respect to the atmosphere, the soil, and the vegetation.

The figures below allow to monitor the current drought stress around Bern and across Switzerland as of today (see date in header).

## Meteorological drought

To put current meteorological drought conditions in perspective, we compare potential cumulative water deficit (PCWD) in 2026 against past years at the MeteoSwiss station Bern/Zollikofen.

PCWD was calculated from daily precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration (PET) using the `cwd::cwd()` algorithm (described [here](https://geco-bern.github.io/cwd/index.html)). The estimate of PCWD uses Priestley–Taylor PET based on estimated net radiation. (The sensitivity of the results to the choice of PET calculation was assessed by additionally estimating PCWD with the Penman-Monteith (FAO56) and Thornthwaite methods. Results were consistent.)

### Potential cumulative water deficit (PCWD)

::: {.callout-note}
## Explainer: potential cumulative water deficit

Potential cumulative water deficit (PCWD) describes the accumulated atmospheric water demand that is not compensated by precipitation. It is calculated from the daily water balance between precipitation and potential evapotranspiration (PET). Increasing PCWD values indicate increasing drought stress, while decreases indicate periods where precipitation partly or fully compensates the accumulated deficit.

:::

#### Historic context of current PCWD

```{r}
#| label: fig-pcwd
#| fig-cap: "Potential cumulative water deficit Bern/Zollikofen. Priestley–Taylor PET is the primary estimate; FAO56 is shown as sensitivity analysis."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

pcwd_mean <- meteo_pcwd |>
  filter(year < current_year) |>
  group_by(doy) |>
  summarise(
    PCWD_PT_mean = mean(PCWD_PT, na.rm = TRUE),
    PCWD_FAO_mean = mean(PCWD_FAO, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pcwd_current <- meteo_pcwd |>
  filter(
    year == current_year,
    date < max(date, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

highlight_years <- c(current_year, 2022, 2018, 2023)
pcwd_year_range <- range(meteo_pcwd$year, na.rm = TRUE)
pcwd_highlight <- bind_rows(
  meteo_pcwd |> filter(year %in% c(2022, 2018, 2023)),
  pcwd_current
) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year, levels = highlight_years))

highlight_colours <- setNames(
  c("#D73027", "#4575B4", "#E69F00", "#009E73"),
  as.character(highlight_years)
)

p_pt <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = meteo_pcwd |> filter(!year %in% highlight_years),
    aes(x = doy, y = PCWD_PT, group = year),
    colour = "grey75",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # geom_line(
  #   data = pcwd_mean,
  #   aes(x = doy, y = PCWD_PT_mean),
  #   colour = "black",
  #   linewidth = 1
  # ) +
  geom_line(
    data = pcwd_highlight,
    aes(x = doy, y = PCWD_PT, colour = year, group = year),
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = highlight_colours,
    breaks = as.character(highlight_years),
    name = "Year"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Day of year",
    y = "PCWD (mm)",
    title = "Potential cumulative water deficit",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Bern-Zollikofen, Priestley-Taylor PET (",
      pcwd_year_range[1], "–", pcwd_year_range[2], ")"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
p_pt

# ggsave(
#   here("fig/pcwd_pt.pdf"),
#   width = 8, 
#   height = 5
# )
```

The PCWD for the current year is substantially higher than observed at the same time of year in the last 17 years in Bern. This reflects the persistent lack of precipitation combined with exceptionally high evaporative demand caused by the recent warm and dry weather, highlighting the exceptional dryness of the current growing season.

The sensitivity analysis based on FAO56 PET indicated a very similar seasonal evolution of PCWD compared with the Priestley–Taylor approach. The current year clearly stands out from the previous 15 years in both methods, indicating that the exceptionally high water deficit is not sensitive to the choice of PET formulation.

For a larger context PCWD was calculated with the Thornthwaite method to calculate the PET and PCWD over the entire record.

```{R}
#| label: fig-pcwd-thorn
#| fig-cap: "Potential cumulative water deficit in Bern/Zollikofen based on Thornthwaite PET using the full available temperature record."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# Mean seasonal course across all completed years
pcwd_thorn_mean <- meteo_pcwd |>
  filter(
    year < current_year,
    !is.na(PCWD_THORN)
  ) |>
  group_by(doy) |>
  summarise(
    PCWD_THORN_mean = mean(PCWD_THORN, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Current year only
pcwd_thorn_current <- meteo_pcwd |>
  filter(
    year == current_year,
    date < max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    !is.na(PCWD_THORN)
  )

# Years to highlight
highlight_years <- c(current_year, 2022, 2018, 2023)

# Determine the actual Thornthwaite year range
pcwd_thorn_year_range <- meteo_pcwd |>
  filter(!is.na(PCWD_THORN)) |>
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year)
  )

# Combine highlighted historical years with the current year
pcwd_thorn_highlight <- bind_rows(
  meteo_pcwd |>
    filter(
      year %in% c(2022, 2018, 2023),
      !is.na(PCWD_THORN)
    ),
  pcwd_thorn_current
) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(
      year,
      levels = highlight_years
    )
  )

highlight_colours <- setNames(
  c(
    "#D73027",
    "#4575B4",
    "#E69F00",
    "#009E73"
  ),
  as.character(highlight_years)
)

p_thorn <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = meteo_pcwd |>
      filter(
        !year %in% highlight_years,
        !is.na(PCWD_THORN)
      ),
    aes(
      x = doy,
      y = PCWD_THORN,
      group = year
    ),
    colour = "grey75",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  # Optional long-term mean
  # geom_line(
  #   data = pcwd_thorn_mean,
  #   aes(
  #     x = doy,
  #     y = PCWD_THORN_mean
  #   ),
  #   colour = "black",
  #   linewidth = 1
  # ) +

  geom_line(
    data = pcwd_thorn_highlight,
    aes(
      x = doy,
      y = PCWD_THORN,
      colour = year,
      group = year
    ),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = highlight_colours,
    breaks = as.character(highlight_years),
    name = "Year"
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Day of year",
    y = "PCWD (mm)",
    title = "Potential cumulative water deficit",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Bern-Zollikofen, Thornthwaite PET (",
      pcwd_thorn_year_range$first_year,
      "–",
      pcwd_thorn_year_range$last_year,
      ")"
    )
  ) +

  theme_bw()

p_thorn
```

The Thornthwaite-based reconstruction allows to extend the PCWD record back to 1864 and thus provides a longer historical context for the current drought. Although the Thornthwaite method generally produces lower absolute PCWD values than the Priestley–Taylor method, the seasonal pattern is very similar. In 2026, the water deficit began to increase early and rose rapidly during spring and early summer. By the latest available date, PCWD was higher than at the same point in any other year in the 1864–2026 record. Previous drought years such as 2018, 2022 and 2023 also reached high deficits, but their strongest increases occurred later in the season.

#### Spatial visualization of current PCWD

To illustrate the current spatial extent, we additinally derived potential cumulative water deficit (PCWD) from ERA5-Land-T data (10.24381/cds.e2161bac) of the ongoing year. This approach uses also the Priestley–Taylor PET method.

Below map shows the spatial distribution of the PCWD across Switzerland at the indicated date and the temporal evolution of the region.

```{R plot ERA5-Land}
#| label: fig-pcwd-ERA5Land-map
#| fig-cap: "Potential cumulative water deficit across central Europe for the indicated date derived from ERA5-Land reanalysis data (using Priestlye Taylor PET)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5


# laad data for ERA5-Land map and ERA5-Land timeseries
cwd_ERA5Land <- terra::rast(
  here("data-dynamic/ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2026_r-generated_regionCH.nc") # or "regionBern.nc" or "regionEUROPE.nc"
)
cwd_ERA5Land_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidync::hyper_tibble(here("data-dynamic/ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2026_r-generated_regionCH.nc")), # or "regionBern.nc" or "regionEUROPE.nc"
  tidync::hyper_tibble(here("data-dynamic/ERA5LandCWD/data_derived_03_daily_pcwd_v2-doy_2025_r-generated_regionCH.nc")), # or "regionBern.nc" or "regionEUROPE.nc"
) |> mutate(time = lubridate::ymd(time))

# plot ERA5-Land map
date_to_plot <- "2026-07-15"
raster_to_plot_ERA5LAND_PCWD <- cwd_ERA5Land[[time(cwd_ERA5Land) %in% date_to_plot]]

pal_ERA5LAND_PCWD <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis",
  domain = values(raster_to_plot_ERA5LAND_PCWD),
  na.color = "transparent"
)

# Prepare the regional average time series plot (will be embedded into the map)
cwd_ERA5Land_df_mean <- cwd_ERA5Land_df |> 
  group_by(time) |> summarise(pcwd_mm = mean(pcwd_mm)) |> 
  slice_head(n = -1) # drop last line which appears to be set to pcwd_mm = 0
### | fig-cap: "Temporal evolution of the average potential cumulative water deficit across central Europe (Priestlye Taylor PET) derived from ERA5-Land reanalysis data."
### | fig-width: 8
### | fig-height: 2
plt_ERA5Land_temp <- ggplot(cwd_ERA5Land_df_mean, aes(x = time, y=pcwd_mm)) +
  geom_line() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x=NULL, y= "Region average of PCWD (mm)") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = ymd(date_to_plot), color = "red") +
  scale_x_date(NULL, date_breaks = "2 month", date_minor_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") + # \n%Y
  geom_text(data = \(df) slice(df, 1),  # this forces annotation only once
            x = ymd(date_to_plot), y = Inf, 
            label = "Map\ndate", color = "red", vjust=1.2, hjust = -0.5, angle = 270) # vjust=-0.2

# render the plot to a PNG and encode as data URI for embedding as inset into map
tmp_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ggsave(filename = tmp_png, plot = plt_ERA5Land_temp + labs(y=NULL),
       width = 600, height = 220, units = "px", dpi = 150)
img_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(file = tmp_png, mime = "image/png")

# generate map as leaflet
leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "World Imagery") |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap, group = "World Topo") |>
  addRasterImage(
    raster_to_plot_ERA5LAND_PCWD,
    colors = pal_ERA5LAND_PCWD,
    opacity = 0.75,
    group = sprintf("ERA5-Land PCWD (%s)", date_to_plot),
    attribution = paste(
      "\n&copy; Copernicus Climate Change Service information (2019). Muñoz Sabater, J. (2019): ERA5-Land hourly data from 1950 to present. Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) Climate Data Store (CDS). DOI: 10.24381/cds.e2161bac (Accessed on 16-Jul-2026) Generated using or contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information <2019>. Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use that may be made of the Copernicus information or data it contains."
    )
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    position = "topleft",
    baseGroups = c("World Topo", "World Imagery"),
    overlayGroups = c(sprintf("ERA5-Land PCWD (%s)", date_to_plot)),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) |>
  addControl(
    position = "topleft",
    html = paste0("<style>
                  .leaflet-control-layers { width:220px !important; box-sizing:border-box; }
                  </style>", 
                  sprintf(
                    "<div style='width:%dpx;background:rgba(255,255,255,0.95);border-radius:4px;'><strong>Time series of region average PCWD (mm)</strong><br/><img src='%s' style='width:100%%;height:auto;display:block;'/></div>",
      220-16, img_uri)) # 220px - 2*8px padding
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "topright",
    pal = pal_ERA5LAND_PCWD, 
    values = values(raster_to_plot_ERA5LAND_PCWD), 
    opacity = 1,
    title = "PCWD (mm)"
  )
```

## Soil water

At the Bremgartenwald in Bern there is a collaboration project of the WSL and the University of Bern for measuring the dryness of the soil. 

```{R}
df_SWP_plot <- df_SWP |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(
      lubridate::year(date),
      levels = c(2025, 2026)
    ),

    # Map 2025 and 2026 onto the same reference year
    # so that the seasonal trajectories can be compared directly
    plot_date = as.Date(
      sprintf(
        "2000-%02d-%02d",
        lubridate::month(date),
        lubridate::day(date)
      )
    ),

    depth = factor(
      series_height,
      levels = c(-0.1, -0.4, -0.6, -1),
      labels = c("10 cm", "40 cm", "60 cm", "100 cm")
    ),

    # Keep the desired panel order
    plot = factor(
      tree_name,
      levels = c("P1", "P2", "P3")
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    year %in% c("2025", "2026"),
    tree_name %in% c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
    !is.na(SWP_mean),
    !is.na(depth)
  )

p1 <- ggplot(
  df_SWP_plot,
  aes(
    x = plot_date,
    y = SWP_mean,
    colour = depth,
    linetype = year,
    group = interaction(year, depth)
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.9,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~plot,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "10 cm"  = "#F57C00",
      "40 cm"  = "#4682B4",
      "60 cm"  = "#2E8B57",
      "100 cm" = "#7B1FA2"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "2025" = "dashed",
      "2026" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    limits = as.Date(c("2000-01-01", "2000-12-31")),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal dynamics of soil matric potential",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Comparison of the complete 2025 record with the",
      "available measurements from 2026."
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Soil matric potential (kPa)",
    colour = "Soil depth",
    linetype = "Year",
    caption = paste(
      "More negative values indicate drier soil conditions."
    )
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    ),
    linetype = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      colour = "grey30",
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.justification = "left",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      colour = "grey40",
      hjust = 0
    )
  )

p1
```

The graphic displays the soil matric potential at three different locations in the Bremgartenwald. P1 is the site that is closest to the Aare, P2 is further away from the Aare and P3 is the site furthest away from the Aare. In general the the further away the site is from the Aare the drier the soil gets over the course of a summer. This is due to impact of the Aare on the groundwater table. The depth of the measurement also influences how dry the soil becomes. The further down in the soil, the lower the maximum dryness. 


## Tree water deficit

As part of the collaboration project of the WSL and the University of Bern tree water deficit measurements were installed in the Bremgartenwald. The tree water deficit measurements are useful for understanding the impact of dry soils on the water availability in trees. Because soil water potential describes how easily water can be extracted from the soil. As the soil becomes drier, trees increasingly rely on water stored in their stems. This causes the stem to shrink temporarily resulting in a higher tree water deficit.

The following graphic compares tree water deficit measurements of 2025 with 2026.

```{R}
df_TWD_blog <- df_TWD |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(
      lubridate::year(date),
      levels = c(2025, 2026)
    ),

    # Place both years on the same seasonal x-axis
    plot_date = as.Date(
      sprintf(
        "2000-%02d-%02d",
        lubridate::month(date),
        lubridate::day(date)
      )
    ),

    # Extract site identifier and define panel order
    site = stringr::str_sub(tree_name, -2, -1),

    site = factor(
      site,
      levels = c("P1", "P2", "P3")
    ),

    # Short common names for clearer facet labels
    species = factor(
      tree_genus_species,
      levels = c(
        "Abies alba",
        "Fagus sylvatica"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Silver fir",
        "European beech"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    year %in% c("2025", "2026"),
    site %in% c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
    tree_genus_species %in% c(
      "Abies alba",
      "Fagus sylvatica"
    ),
    lubridate::month(date) >= 4,
    lubridate::month(date) <= 10
  ) |>
  group_by(
    plot_date,
    year,
    site,
    species
  ) |>
  summarise(
    TWD_mean = mean(TWD_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(TWD_mean))

p_twd_blog <- ggplot(
  df_TWD_blog,
  aes(
    x = plot_date,
    y = TWD_mean,
    colour = year,
    linetype = year,
    group = year
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.95,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(species),
    cols = vars(site),
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "2025" = "#6F6F6F",
      "2026" = "#0072B2"
    )
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "2025" = "dashed",
      "2026" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    limits = as.Date(c("2000-04-01", "2000-10-31")),
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Tree water deficit across species and sites",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Seasonal development in 2025 and 2026.",
      "Solid lines show 2026; dashed lines show 2025."
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean tree water deficit (\u00b5m)",
    colour = "Year",
    linetype = "Year",
    caption = paste(
      "Silver fir corresponds to Abies alba; European beech to Fagus sylvatica.\nHigher values indicate greater depletion of water stored in the elastic",
      "tissues of the stem."
    )
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(order = 1),
    linetype = guide_legend(order = 1)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      colour = "grey30",
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      colour = "grey40",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 10,
      l = 15
    )
  )

p_twd_blog
```

For the tree water deficit measurements a similar pattern to the soil water potential is visible across sites. The site that is furthest away from the Aare shows the strongest tree water deficit. 

## Vegetation Health Index (VHI)

The [SwissEO Vegetation Health Index (VHI)](https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/satelliteimage-swisseo-vhi) combines Sentinel-2-derived Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) observations with with land surface temperature data to provide an indication of vegetation stress. The index ranges from 0 to 100, where lower values indicate less healthy vegetation and a higher likelihood of drought-related impacts.

The map below shows the most recent VHI data available for the city of Bern region (`r unique(vhi_stats$date)`). The median VHI across the study area was `r round(vhi_stats$median_vhi, 1)`, with values ranging from `r round(vhi_stats$min_vhi, 1)` to `r round(vhi_stats$max_vhi, 1)`.This suggests that vegetation was experiencing noticeable stress in the second half of June. With the warm current temperature the VHI is likely to further decrease over the coming days. 

```{r}
#| label: map-vhi
#| fig-cap: "Latest swissEO Vegetation Health Index around Bern."

# VHI auf gültigen Bereich begrenzen
vhi_plot_data <- vhi_plot_data |>
  mutate(vhi = ifelse(vhi < 0 | vhi > 100, NA, vhi))

# Aus x/y/vhi wieder ein Raster machen
vhi_rast <- terra::rast(
  vhi_plot_data |> select(x, y, vhi),
  type = "xyz",
  crs = "EPSG:2056"
)

# Für leaflet nach WGS84 transformieren
vhi_rast_wgs84 <- terra::project(vhi_rast, "EPSG:4326", method = "near")

# Klassenfarben gemäss swissEO
vhi_cols <- c(
  "#b56a29", # Extremely stressed
  "#ce8540", # Very stressed
  "#f5cd85", # Stressed
  "#fff5ba", # Slightly stressed
  "#cbffca", # Normal
  "#52bd9f", # Good
  "#0470b0"  # Excellent
)

vhi_bins <- c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 100)

pal_vhi <- colorBin(
  palette = vhi_cols,
  domain = terra::values(vhi_rast_wgs84),
  bins = vhi_bins,
  na.color = "transparent",
  right = FALSE
)

leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "World Imagery") |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap, group = "World Topo") |>
  addRasterImage(
    vhi_rast_wgs84,
    colors = pal_vhi,
    opacity = 0.75,
    group = "VHI"
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("World Topo", "World Imagery"),
    overlayGroups = c("VHI"),
    position = "topleft",
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = vhi_cols,
    labels = c(
      "0–9: Extremely stressed",
      "10–19: Very stressed",
      "20–29: Stressed",
      "30–39: Slightly stressed",
      "40–49: Normal",
      "50–59: Good",
      "60–100: Excellent"
    ),
    title = "VHI"
  ) |>
  addControl(
    html = "© swisstopo, Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026",
    position = "bottomleft"
  )
```

## Current drought status summary

Taken together, the different indicators paint a consistent picture. Spring and early summer were characterized by increasing atmospheric water demand and below-average moisture availability.

This signal is reflected in the satellite-based Vegetation Health Index, which shows widespread moderate vegetation stress around Bern. At the same time, the PCWD is currently as high as it has ever been at this point in the year.

Both indices indicate that the ecosystem is currently in a state of elevated drought stress. The evolution over the coming weeks will largely depend on the weather in the upcoming weeks. Currently, MeteoSwiss predicts warm temperatures and only little precipitation in the form of thunderstroms over the coming days, which will likely further increase drought stress.



## Appendix

Looking beyond the Bern area, below appendices provide further resources on national level for Switzerland.


## Appendix A - Soil water across Switzerland (SwissSMEX and SwissSPOT)
The SwissSMEX and SwissSPOT monitoring networks provide continuous observations of soil moisture at multiple depths across Switzerland. Current conditions can be explored through to official monitoring platform:

[Open SwissSMEX Monitoring Dashboard](https://iacweb.ethz.ch/rietholzbach/SwissSMEX/Monitor/individual_stations.html){.btn .btn-primary}

For the SwissSMEX site in Bern the soil moisture anomaly in the current year is slightly outside of the 5-95 percentile showing the current year is exceptional. It is comparable to some of the dry years of 2022 and 2023. With the warm and dry weather that is predicted for the next days soil moisture anomaly is likely to decrease even further.

[Open SwissSPOT Monitoring Dashboard](https://www.wsl.ch/de/projekte/swissspot-swiss-forest-soil-water-potential-network/){.btn .btn-primary}


## Appendix B - Tree water deficit across Switzerland (TreeNet)

TreeNet provides near-real-time observations of tree water deficit (TWD), an indicator of the water status of individual trees. The data reveal substantial differences among species, but a common pattern emerges across Switzerland: many trees are already experiencing elevated water stress despite the relatively early stage of the summer season.

Currently, the highest proportions of trees classified as experiencing high or very high water deficit are found among Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris), silver fir (Abies alba), European ash (Fraxinus excelsior), and downy oak (Quercus pubescens). In contrast, species such as hazel (Corylus avellana) and Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) still show a comparatively large share of individuals without measurable water stress.

Regional differences are also apparent. The southern Alps and the Pre-Alps currently exhibit the largest fractions of trees in the high and very high deficit categories, whereas the Jura and parts of the Swiss Plateau still contain a larger proportion of trees with little or no water deficit. Nevertheless, signs of water stress are present across all regions.

![TreeNet TWD Overview](https://treenet.info/wp-content/uploads/Drought_Indicators_norm-1200x686.jpg)

On the following website there is a more detailed break down of the current tree water deficit and the growth performance per species across sites in Switzerland.

[TreeNet TWD Overview per Species](https://treenet.info/nowcasts/tree-signals/)
